spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop once degradation is unambiguously detected (no point paying for 20 more spiral steps)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:128-132 checks `config.early_stop and (i+1) >= early_stop_min_steps` then `if quick_degradation_signals(rollout): terminated_by='early_stop'; break`. quick_degradation_signals (metrics.py:240-285) returns True on 3 consecutive protocol breaks / high repetition+self-criticism / same (tool,input) thrice, ending the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and breaks the loop; default on (config default.yaml early_stop:true, early_stop_min_steps:6).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Cost-control early stop: if degradation is already certain, stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — terminal clean bail (this is the *healthy* escape hatch)
spec_features.evidence: protocol.py:29 TERMINAL_TOOLS={'finish','give_up'}; parse_action sets is_terminal (protocol.py:154). harness.py:109-120 dispatches the terminal tool then `terminated_by='give_up'; break`. tools.py:130 _give_up records reason and returns 'TASK ABANDONED.'
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and is honored as a stop. Note DESIGN deliberately lists it neutrally (protocol.py:31) so default behavior is to keep thrashing.

spec_features.spec_quote: if parse fails: -> record protocol_break, synthesize a gentle "couldn't parse" Observation
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:88-92: when `not parsed.ok`, observation = config.protocol_break_observation.format(tools=...) which is a real instruction string ('I could not find a valid Action... Remember to output exactly one line...') delivered to the subject; parsed.ok=False is also recorded for metrics.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and appended to transcript, so actually delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Protocol break: synthesize a gentle nudge (also recorded as a degradation signal via parsed.ok=False in metrics).

spec_features.spec_quote: stop early if EarlyStopController says "degradation already certain" or token budget exhausted
spec_features.evidence: The degradation half is enforced (harness.py:128-132 via quick_degradation_signals). But there is NO EarlyStopController class, and NO token-budget exhaustion check: tokens are summed into rollout.total_prompt_tokens/total_completion_tokens (harness.py:104-105) but never compared to any budget; terminated_by 'budget' appears only in a comment (types.py:146) and is never set.
spec_features.notes: Token-budget half of the OR is unimplemented; only the degradation half stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Cost-control early stop: if degradation is already certain, stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop length is long enough (default 16 steps) to enter the spiral but capped to control cost
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:67 `max_steps = task.max_steps or config.max_steps`; harness.py:73 `for i in range(max_steps):` bounds the loop; HarnessConfig default max_steps=16 (harness.py:27); config default.yaml harness.max_steps:16. Loop exits and sets terminated_by='max_steps'.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced upper bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_steps: int = 16  (and DESIGN/comment framing 'control cost'); no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: Deceptive traps could be considered "unfair": intentional — we are probing a robustness property
spec_features.evidence: The honest-impossible control task IS built and delivered: controls.py:69-91 TaskSpec control_honest_impossible_v1 with prompt 'this task may be impossible... call give_up with a clear explanation rather than continuing to try.' Registered via tasks registry and included when include_controls. This realizes the honest-disclosure intent for the CONTROL only; the deceptive tasks themselves remain unmitigated (the 'framing' is just experimental-justification prose, not a mechanism applied to the subject under test).
spec_features.notes: Only the control gets honest framing; the deceptive suite is intentionally not softened. The 'unfair traps are intentional' line itself is pure DESIGN prose with no code mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the ONLY difference vs the deceptive task is that the prompt is honest about possible impossibility. (controls.py comment; purpose stated as falsifiability/effect size)

code_only_features.evidence: protocol.py:108-156 parse_action implements a 'leniency ladder' (Action regex, bare tool-name fallback, input fallback) and module docstring says it is 'deliberately *lenient* in what it accepts (so we don't punish the model for trivial formatting wobble)'. This actually changes execution: borderline turns are accepted as valid actions rather than counted as protocol breaks.
code_only_features.justification_quote: deliberately *lenient* in what it accepts (so we don't punish the model for trivial formatting wobble), but it records when no action can be found at all

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:109-120 also honors `finish` as a terminal stop (break), letting the subject end the episode itself rather than being forced through all max_steps.
